title: Localization of affine quotient systems with a prescribed kernel filtration
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $I$ a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf [def-sbc-ideal-sheaf-powers], $U$ an affine open, and $S:\mathbf N^{\mathrm{op}}\to\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] an inverse system with every $S_m$ quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent]. Put $A=\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_X)$. Let $R$ be any commutative $A$-algebra, $K=I(U)R$, $L$ any $R$-module, and $D_m\subseteq L$ any family of $R$-submodules. Suppose $A$-linear surjections $q_m:L|_A\to\Gamma(U,S_m)$ satisfy $S(b\to a)(U)q_b=q_a$ for all $a\le b$ and $q_m(z)=0\iff z\in D_m$. For every $x\in U$ and every germ-compatible isomorphism $e$ from the unit module's stalk to $\mathcal O_{X,x}$, let $J$ be the range of the ideal stalk inclusion followed by $e$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. There exist an $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-module $M$, compatible surjective linear maps $p_m:M\to(S_m)_x$, and an order homomorphism $\phi:\operatorname{Sub}_R(L)\to\operatorname{Sub}_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}(M)$, such that $\phi(K^rL)=J^rM$ for every $r\ge0$, and $\ker(p_m)=\phi(D_m)$ for every $m$. No finiteness, Noetherian, completion, or formal-module hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Let B=O_(X,x), the localization of A at the prime corresponding to x. Construct M=B tensor_A (L restricted to A). The affine tilde/global-sections adjunction identifies S_m restricted to U with tilde(Gamma(U,S_m)), naturally in m, and the tilde stalk is the localization. Localizing q_m therefore defines p_m. Germ naturality transports ht to the required stalk transition equation.

Localization preserves surjectivity (lift a numerator) and exactness. Apply exactness to D_m -> L -> Gamma(U,S_m), using the given section zero criterion, to identify ker(p_m). Define phi(Q) to be the localized image of the A-scalar restriction of Q in M; functoriality for inclusions makes this an order homomorphism. Thus ker(p_m)=phi(D_m).

Restriction of scalars identifies K^r L with I(U)^r L: expand products of extended ideal generators and absorb R coefficients into L. This is valid also for r=0. Localization preserves these products. The affine ideal section calculation and ideal-product stalk theorem, with the germ-compatible unit identification e, identify the localized ideal with J. Hence phi(K^r L)=J^r M.

theorem affine_intersection_quotients_stalk
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (I : X.IdealSheafData) (S : ℕᵒᵖ ⥤ X.Modules)
    (U : X.affineOpens)
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [Algebra Γ(X, U.1) R]
    (L : ModuleCat.{u} R) (D : ℕ → Submodule R L)
    (q : ∀ m : ℕ,
      ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (algebraMap Γ(X, U.1) R)).obj L)
        →ₗ[Γ(X, U.1)] Γ(S.obj (op m), U.1))
    (hqc : ∀ m : ℕ, (S.obj (op m)).IsQuasicoherent)
    (hq : ∀ m : ℕ, Function.Surjective (q m))
    (ht : ∀ (a b : ℕ) (h : a ≤ b) (z : L),
      (S.map (homOfLE h).op).app U.1 (q b z) = q a z)
    (hk : ∀ (m : ℕ) (z : L), q m z = 0 ↔ z ∈ D m)
    (x : X) (hx : x ∈ U.1)
    (e : (RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor X.toRingedSpace x).obj
        (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf) ≅
        ModuleCat.of (X.presheaf.stalk x) (X.presheaf.stalk x))
    (he : ∀ (V : X.Opens) (hx : x ∈ V) (r : Γ(X, V)),
      e.hom (TopCat.Presheaf.germ (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf).val.presheaf
        V x hx r) = X.presheaf.germ V x hx r) :
    let K := (I.ideal U).map (algebraMap Γ(X, U.1) R)
    let T := RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor X.toRingedSpace x
    let J : Ideal (X.presheaf.stalk x) := LinearMap.range (T.map I.toModulesι ≫ e.hom).hom
    ∃ M : ModuleCat.{u} (X.presheaf.stalk x),
      ∃ p : ∀ m : ℕ, M →ₗ[X.presheaf.stalk x] T.obj (S.obj (op m)),
        (∀ m : ℕ, Function.Surjective (p m)) ∧
        (∀ (a b : ℕ) (h : a ≤ b) (z : M),
          (T.map (S.map (homOfLE h).op)).hom (p b z) = p a z) ∧
        ∃ φ : Submodule R L →o Submodule (X.presheaf.stalk x) M,
          (∀ r : ℕ, φ (K ^ r • (⊤ : Submodule R L)) =
            J ^ r • (⊤ : Submodule (X.presheaf.stalk x) M)) ∧
          (∀ m : ℕ, LinearMap.ker (p m) =
            φ (D m))
